In [[differential geometry]], a branch of [[mathematics]], a '''Riemannian submersion''' is a [[Submersion (mathematics)|submersion]] from one [[Riemannian manifold]] to another that respects the metrics, meaning that it is an [[orthogonal projection]] on tangent spaces.

== Formal definition ==
Let (''M'', ''g'') and (''N'', ''h'') be two Riemannian manifolds and <math>f:M\to N</math> a (surjective) submersion, i.e., a [[fibered manifold]]. The horizontal distribution <math>\mathrm{ker}(df)^{\perp}</math> is a [[fiber bundle|sub-bundle]] of the [[tangent bundle]] of <math>TM</math> which depends both on the projection <math>f</math> and on the metric <math>g</math>. The expression <math>\mathrm{ker}(df)^{\perp}</math> denotes the subbundle of <math>TM</math> that is the orthogonal complement of <math>\mathrm{ker}(df_x) \sub T_{x}M</math> at each point x of ''M''.

Then, ''f'' is called a Riemannian submersion if and only if, for all <math>x\in M</math>, the vector space isomorphism <math>(df)_x : \mathrm{ker}(df_x)^{\perp} \rightarrow T_{f(x)}N</math> is an isometry, or in other words it carries each vector to one of the same length.<ref>{{Citation|title=Spinors, Spectral Geometry, and Riemannian Submersions|first1=Peter B.|last1=Gilkey|first2=John V.|last2=Leahy|first3=Jeonghyeong|last3=Park|url=http://www.emis.de/monographs/GLP/|year=1998|publisher=Global Analysis Research Center, Seoul National University|pages=4–5}}</ref>

==Examples==
An example of a Riemannian submersion arises when a [[Lie group]] <math>G</math> acts isometrically, [[free action|freely]] and [[proper action|properly]] on a Riemannian manifold <math>(M,g)</math>. 
The projection <math>\pi: M \rightarrow N</math> to the [[Quotient space (topology)|quotient space]] <math>N = M /G</math> equipped with the quotient metric is a Riemannian submersion.
For example, component-wise multiplication on <math>S^3 \subset  \mathbb{C}^2</math> by the group of unit complex numbers yields the [[Hopf fibration]].

==Properties==
The sectional curvature of the target space of a Riemannian submersion can be calculated from the curvature of the total space by '''O'Neill's formula''', named for [[Barrett O'Neill]]:
:<math>K_N(X,Y)=K_M(\tilde X, \tilde Y)+\tfrac34|[\tilde X,\tilde Y]^V|^2</math>
where <math>X,Y</math> are orthonormal vector fields on <math>N</math>, <math>\tilde X, \tilde Y</math> their horizontal lifts to <math>M</math>, <math>[*,*]</math> is the [[Lie bracket of vector fields]] and <math>Z^V</math> is the projection of the vector field <math>Z</math> to the [[Vertical and horizontal bundles|vertical distribution]].

In particular the lower bound for the sectional curvature of <math>N</math> is at least as big as the lower bound for the sectional curvature of <math>M</math>.
